questions.q: What does the CIA triad stand for in data security?
options: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability
Collection, Identification, Access
Consent, Information, Accountability
Classification, Inventory, Audit
questions.explain: The CIA triad is the standard model for data security: confidentiality (only authorized access), integrity (accurate, untampered data), and availability (accessible to legitimate users when needed).

questions.q: Which question does data privacy ask that data security does not?
options: Whether the data is encrypted in transit
Whether the person's data was collected and used with their knowledge and consent
Whether the database has a current backup
Whether the server has the latest security patch
questions.explain: Security protects data regardless of how it was obtained or why. Privacy asks whether collecting and using that data was appropriate in the first place — notice, consent, and purpose.

questions.q: Which scenario best illustrates a system that is secure but still violates privacy?
options: A database with no password that anyone can read
A strongly encrypted, access-controlled database that collects and uses personal data without the person's knowledge or consent
A server that loses data because of a missing backup
A report that contains an inaccurate sales figure
questions.explain: Encryption and access control address confidentiality, not whether collecting or using the data was appropriate. A fully locked-down system can still violate privacy if it uses personal data in ways the person never agreed to.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why is a privacy-respecting policy 'worthless without security behind it'?
options: Because privacy policies are legally unenforceable everywhere
Because security software is required by law in every country
Because without access controls and protection, the policy's promises can't actually be enforced — anyone can read the underlying data
Because privacy and security always require the exact same controls
questions.explain: A policy describing careful, consented data use means nothing in practice if the data it describes isn't actually protected — security is what makes privacy promises real rather than just words on a page.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what topic does the course cover immediately after this introductory lesson on security and privacy concepts?
options: Data classification labels (public/internal/confidential/restricted)
PII — personally identifiable information
Access control models
SOX and industry-specific regulations
questions.explain: The lesson previews the course roadmap: PII comes next (Lesson 2), followed by sensitive/confidential data, the major regulations, privacy by design, classification, access control, protection methods, lifecycle/compliance, and case studies.
